observations.content: Subagent sisyphus completed the fallow quality refactor in the recipebook workspace: removed InterruptError.exitCode (inlined process.exit(130) in runCliCommand), de-exported printCancel in packages/cli/src/cli/errors.ts, de-exported selectRegistryPacks and RegistryItemSelection in packages/core/src/plan.ts, extracted createScriptLoadModule helper shared by both script executors in packages/core/src/scripts.ts, and split renderRow into renderGroupHeader/renderItemRow in packages/cli/src/cli/prompts.ts. Verification: pnpm run quality exit 0, pnpm run check passes, tests pass (core 415/415, cli 342/342).

Assistant spawned subagent vader to verify sisyphus's refactor and try to break it, with instructions to inspect diffs, grep for orphaned references, and independently run pnpm test and pnpm run quality.

Vader completed with verdict held: no reproducible break. Diff was exactly the 4 claimed files (53+/49-), no removed symbol is on any package entry point, grep found zero remaining references, both acceptance commands pass with expected counts, typecheck and biome clean. A clean-tree control (git stash) confirmed quality exited 1 before the refactor. One non-breaking observation: fallow-baselines/ (dead-code.json, dupes.json) are now stale and emit warnings in pnpm run quality:changes, exit 0, harmless hygiene item.

Assistant ran graphify update . per project rules (graphify-out/graph.json exists); graph rebuilt with 855 nodes, 1872 edges, 54 communities. Noted optional follow-up of regenerating stale fallow baselines. Also noted warning that the installed graphify skill is 0.9.50 vs package 0.9.63, and community labels need refresh via graphify label.
User asked for maintainability at 100 as well, and to also improve the fallow complexity and hotspots.

Assistant gathered full fallow health data (fallow v3.16.0): avg MI 91.7 across 58 files, 0 functions above threshold, health_score 78.3 grade B with penalties hotspots 10.0, unit_size 10.0 (3.4% functions > 60 LOC, functions_over_60_loc_per_k 33.6), coupling 1.7; 2 churn hotspots. Lowest-MI files include packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts (85.4), commands/add.ts (87.0), commands/index.ts (87.1), core/scripts.ts (87.1), core/parse.ts (87.3), core/plan.ts (87.4), core/handlers.ts (87.5).

Assistant spawned subagent aristotle to choose the approach for the maintainability refactor, researching fallow docs at docs.fallow.tools/explanations/health for the MI formula and hotspot definitions, and writing a plan to .cursor/scratch/maintainability-100.md.
Aristotle's first run failed after 1m31s with a transient connection error; assistant resumed the session via subagent_message with the original task.

Aristotle completed and wrote its plan to .cursor/scratch/maintainability-100.md. Recommendation: reject the literal maintainability_avg=100 target as mathematically impossible. Validated fallow per-file MI formula from docs in node_modules/fallow (accurate within ±1 across 10 files): MI = 100 − 30·(cyclo/LOC) − 20·dead_ratio − 4·ln(fan_out+1). Any file with ≥1 import caps at 97.2; all real files import 5–10 sources. Even avg 95 would require inverting the whole import graph, rejected as a rewrite violating AGENTS.md and risking 757 tests. Proposed target: health_score 100/grade A by zeroing hotspots, unit_size, and coupling penalties, with avg MI rising to ~93. Concrete actions: split the two hotspot files (cli/commands/index.ts, cli/prompts.ts) to churn-free new paths, split all ~37 functions >60 LOC via fallow's large_functions[] drill-down, then cheap fan-out/density trims in add.ts/parse.ts.

Assistant presented aristotle's plan to the user and stopped for approval: the key trade-off is accepting ~93 avg MI (not 100, not 95) with health_score 100/A as primary metric. Risks flagged: fresh churn re-flagging split hotspots, test-splitting weakening test intent, undocumented penalty thresholds.
User approved the plan with "Sure" — proceed with target health_score 100/A and avg MI ~93, meaning implementation can begin.
